title: Metaphor
subtitle: The color of sacrifice, the color of symbolism, a color that never fades.

items.text: The man shows no fear as he turns toward the assassin.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: What do you make of this? Are we to have some sort of puppet master's tea party?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: You figured this all out some time ago, didn't you?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: I did. But there is still some satisfaction in watching the dominoes fall, even when you know where they'll land. A little more shock would've been welcome, though.
The two of them speak with the same casual ease.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Pray, begin then.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Let's start with the mural. Look at the symbolism.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: In Aztec mythology, hummingbirds and butterflies represent death and rebirth.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Fallen warriors entered the realm of the sun god. After four years, they would be reborn as butterflies and hummingbirds, returning to drink the eternal nectar of the earth.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: To Muriel, his fellow artists of the Midnight Kitchen were like those brave warriors, destined to return, having transcended death.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Spot on.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: This circle of hummingbirds and butterflies in the mural represents ten reborn souls.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: But if you look closely ...

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: There are only nine figures in the mural: the seven victims, Muriel, and Ramona.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: So, where's the tenth? Did Muriel hide them away somewhere?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: That's exactly what he did. It's quite clever, really, merging a metaphor, or a pun, if you will, into the mural.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Everyone, including Muriel, calls you Añil.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Añil, the name of a plant native to southern Mexico used to create a rich indigo dye. Over time, it also became the name for that deep, vibrant shade of blue.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: For centuries before the arrival of the Europeans, indigenous peoples used it to dye the cloaks of their leaders. Like Tyrrhenian red, this deep indigo blue symbolized power in their culture.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: And behold, that very color is hidden in this mural. The rivers and trees in the background glow with its intensity.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Muriel used that blue añil to paint those sections, blending your presence into the mural in the most conspicuous yet subtle way.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Muriel wasn't the only member of the Midnight Kitchen to cross the "Storm," was he?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: There was another artist of the Midnight Kitchen who went to Europe with him.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: That artist was you, Añil.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: And?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Like Muriel, I survived the "Storms." What does it matter?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Oh, it matters in many ways.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Those victims, your handpicked vessels, were all arcanists who bore some resemblance to the friends you lost in the "Storm."

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: You lured them to the Turquoise Serpent Club and presented each with a meticulously crafted gift, a painting that would become their death warrant.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: True, Muriel was a genius in arcanum. He single-handedly devised a resurrection ritual based on Roseau's research and ancient legends.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: But with every painting he completed, he lost fragments of his memory. A flawed method.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: In the end, he was no longer whole.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: How could he have planned and executed all this, alone, in such a state?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Finding eight suitable targets among hundreds of thousands in Mexico City, coaxing them to accept paintings they probably had no interest in.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Each step required meticulous observation and careful planning.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: It was all you pulling the strings, Añil. A pigment dealer kidnapped by gangsters? Just a cover.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: The most brilliant part is that you orchestrated this entire series of murders just to bring Ramona to center stage!
She laughs softly but without a trace of warmth.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Haha. You watched her, studied her nature, leveraged her hatred of injustice and her love for this city.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: You lured her to this mural, intending to offer her as the final sacrifice to fulfill your ultimate wish.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: But I still have one question.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Please, ask it. I'll not hold my tongue.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: You completed every step, executed every detail according to your plan. You could have succeeded. So, why didn't you stop me?
His response is muted. There's almost a hint of surprise, but it rests beneath his calm composure.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: That's all you want to ask? I see.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Your deductions are perfect, of course, Ms. Butterfly. I am merely an amateur by comparison.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: In the past four years, Muriel and I have survived six "Storms."

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: As more "Storms" fell, returning to Mexico City to find suitable candidates grew increasingly difficult.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: To put our full focus into our resurrection research, we left Manus Vindictae, not that they had any use for two unmanageable pawns anyway.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Time and again, our work was interrupted by the "Storm," and the ritual's results were never promising to begin with.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I observed each candidate carefully, searching for some trace of our lost friends' souls.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: But the closer I looked, the clearer it became: They weren't the same.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Ramona, for instance, was in many ways the perfect candidate. And yet, she wasn't Teresita. She could never be Teresita.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: The mentor we all admired, the friend who brought warmth and light into our often bleak lives—she was gone. And nothing we did could bring her back.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: *sigh* Ramona's story, however, isn't over. Her future, her dreams, her fierce love for this city ... I realized I couldn't bring myself to destroy that.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: That's all.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: That's all? Really?
Her doubt is written plain on her face, but Añil can only smile bitterly.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: My answer disappoints you. Allow me to put it another way.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: The "Storms" have carried me across time, even into the future. And there, I saw the tedious repetition of human history.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: And the hollow, meaningless cycle of our pursuits. In the end, art cannot change the world.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Our ideal of reshaping society for the better through fine arts eventually became just another capitalist venture, a product, another ignoble chapter in the history of art.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: And my partner, my last remaining friend, lost himself along the way.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I've walked this tortuous path alone for a long, long time.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I'm tired.
Doubt turns to annoyance. This web of intrigue once again turns out to be nothing more than a cat's cradle, child's play to unravel.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Tch, what a disappointment.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: I would have hoped people like us never get tired.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: "People like us"? *chuckle* I'm honored to be considered among the likes of you.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: But enough about me, Ms. Butterfly. Would you care to talk about yourself a bit?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Me?
The playful light leaves her eyes. The man notices but continues anyway.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: On our way to the auction, just before we teleported via that Sun Stone.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I realized you couldn't distinguish certain colors, even ones that appear quite different to most.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I imagine that's why you couldn't crack the case earlier.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: It must have taken you considerable effort to discern that the most critical clue lay in the painting's colors.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: You've uncovered a minor flaw of mine. Do you intend to threaten me with it?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: If I'm honest, I'm not entirely sure.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: What if my name were a color you couldn't recognize? How very fortunate you were that I was named Añil.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: It may be a "minor" flaw, as you say, something easily concealed.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: But someone as meticulous as you would never allow anyone to know of it, be they friend or enemy.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: I could kill you to keep this quiet. Did you consider that?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: You won't.
The threat of death washes over him without effect.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: You crave total control. You need to perfectly discern your target's mind, predict their every move, before you pull the trigger.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: You enjoy playing god, holding all the cards, so that life and death become yours to give. You won't kill me until you've mapped out every crevice of my mind.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Impressive, Añil.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: I'll be sure to keep your insights in mind.
She emphasizes her words and extends a hand to him in as earnest a gesture as she can offer.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Guess we'll be keeping our little secrets between us.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: With pleasure. If you need anything regarding the Manus, information, items, reach out to me. I'll do my best to assist.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: And please, take this. My gift.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Use it sparingly.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: It's no easy task to craft this pigment now.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Ha, your contribution to science is appreciated.
